audits.title: 39 An audit of Vitamin D status in acute medical patients over the age of 65
audits.standard: Department of Health guidance 2020: adults over 65 should take 15 micrograms vitamin D daily
audits.setting: Acute medical patients over 65, Wexford General Hospital

cycle1.result: 48% not on any vitamin D supplement; 64% insufficient (32% deficient), of whom 44% not on vitamin D; vitamin D result mentioned in 18% of discharge letters.

audits.other_findings: 30% presented with fractures, and 10% of those were not on vitamin D.
audits.citation: Coelho D, O'Sullivan E. 39 An audit of Vitamin D status in acute medical patients over the age of 65. Age and Ageing. 2023;52(Supplement_3). doi:10.1093/ageing/afad156.069.

audits.title: Vitamin D deficiency in a high secure forensic psychiatry hospital: A clinical audit and service evaluation
audits.standard: Local trust guideline: vitamin D checked within one month of admission and then three-monthly, with dosing by level
audits.setting: Broadmoor Hospital, high secure forensic psychiatry hospital, 15 wards

cycle1.result: 76.4% checked within one month of admission; 66.7% checked in last 3 months; 21.4% correct dose, 22.9% under-dosed, 14.3% over-dosed, 41.4% no dose when indicated

audits.other_findings: Deficiency fell from 43.6% at admission to 14.5% on most recent levels.
audits.citation: Gillett G, Chudleigh-Warren S, Hardy B, Gordon C. Vitamin D deficiency in a high secure forensic psychiatry hospital: A clinical audit and service evaluation. BJPsych Open. 2021;7(Suppl 1):S26-S26.

audits.title: 37 RE-AUDIT OF VITAMIN D SUPPLEMENTATION IN FRAIL OLDER ADULTS PRESENTING TO AN IRISH LEVEL 5 EMERGENCY DEPARTMENT
audits.standard: Department of Health 2020 guidance: all adults 65 and over supplemented with 15 micrograms vitamin D daily
audits.setting: Frailty Intervention Team, level 5 emergency department, Mater Misericordiae University Hospital, Dublin
audits.intervention: Policy update and education after the initial audit.

cycle2.result: Compliance 61% (n=40); 68% (n=45) prescribed vitamin D, of whom 89% (n=40) at least 15 micrograms; 32% (n=21) none; 8% (n=5) lower doses.

audits.other_findings: Median Clinical Frailty Score 5; results felt to reflect community prescribing rather than acute practice.
audits.citation: Pender C, O'Caheny C, Byrne C, Magner S, Carey S, Carrabine N, et al.. 37 RE-AUDIT OF VITAMIN D SUPPLEMENTATION IN FRAIL OLDER ADULTS PRESENTING TO AN IRISH LEVEL 5 EMERGENCY DEPARTMENT. Age and Ageing. 2022;51(Supplement_3). doi:10.1093/ageing/afac218.029.

audits.title: P49 An audit of baseline vitamin D level tests for newly diagnosed paediatric haematology/oncology patients against trust guidelines
audits.standard: Trust guideline for vitamin D deficiency: 100% tested at diagnosis; 100% of results acted on; 100% given appropriate dose
audits.setting: Paediatric haematology/oncology; new diagnoses of malignant disease

cycle1.result: 56% tested for vitamin D during admission; 35% of oncology and 83% of haematology patients tested. 6% of haematology and 5% of oncology patients with sufficient levels received treatment not indicated; the 5% of oncology patients with insufficient levels were not treated. Standards not met.

audits.other_findings: Recommendations: follow the revised trust guideline, pharmacists to check vitamin D for all new admissions, and build a default test into the new prescribing system.
audits.citation: Samrin-Balch L, Mahmood S. P49 An audit of baseline vitamin D level tests for newly diagnosed paediatric haematology/oncology patients against trust guidelines. Archives of Disease in Childhood. 2020;105(9):e32-e33. doi:10.1136/archdischild-2020-nppg.58.

audits.title: Investigation and management of vitamin D insufficiency and deficiency in acute adult psychiatric admissions: a clinical audit
audits.standard: Trust policy: vitamin D checked in all inpatients and supplementation started where appropriate; target 90% for both
audits.setting: Becklin Centre, acute adult psychiatric inpatient unit (four wards), Leeds and York Partnership NHS Foundation Trust

cycle1.result: Vitamin D checked in 79 (56.4%); colecalciferol started in 61 (83.6%) of those insufficient or deficient. Target not met.

audits.other_findings: Testing differed by ethnicity (Caucasian 64.0% vs non-Caucasian 44.4%, p = 0.032) but replacement did not; 92.4% of those tested were insufficient or deficient.
audits.citation: Romeu D, Sood R, Hughes R, Mahmood T, Cardno A. Investigation and management of vitamin D insufficiency and deficiency in acute adult psychiatric admissions: a clinical audit. BJPsych Open. 2021;7(Suppl 1):S101-S101.

audits.title: An audit of vitamin D monitoring and management of deficiency in women's secure services
audits.standard: Trust guideline for management of vitamin D deficiency
audits.setting: Women's secure services, Ardenleigh, Birmingham and Solihull Mental Health NHS Foundation Trust

cycle1.result: 89% had vitamin D checked; 25% of those within 1 week of admission; 89% needing treatment prescribed supplementation, 94% at correct dose and duration

audits.title: Audit of Current Vitamin D Testing on Bridge House Detoxification Unit
audits.standard: NICE PH56: test and replace vitamin D in adults at high risk of deficiency

cycle1.result: No patient had vitamin D tested (0%).

audits.intervention: Pre-populated admission blood form including vitamin D, used on the first day of admission.

cycle2.result: Compliance maintained at 90% in the third round.

audits.other_findings: Three rounds with 76 patients in total; round two achieved 86.67%. Of 44 tested after the change, 30 (68.18%) were deficient or inadequate.
audits.citation: Ayanda S, Felix F, Braithwaite S, McCloud A. Audit of Current Vitamin D Testing on Bridge House Detoxification Unit. BJPsych Open. 2024;10(S1):S215-S216. doi:10.1192/bjo.2024.534.

audits.title: Prophylactic Vitamin D Prescribing for Adult Inpatients on Psychiatric Wards at Warneford Hospital – an Audit
audits.standard: Local Trust guidelines: all adult inpatients offered year-round vitamin D prophylaxis unless osteomalacia symptoms
audits.setting: Three adult psychiatric inpatient wards (2 female, 1 male), Warneford Hospital

cycle1.result: 8 (16%) prescribed prophylactic vitamin D; male ward 1 (6%).

audits.intervention: Trust guidelines reformatted into a simplified poster and flow chart distributed to ward doctors' offices.

cycle2.result: 16 (31%) prescribed prophylactic vitamin D; male ward 5 (28%).

audits.other_findings: Ward populations changed between measurements because of normal admissions and discharges.
audits.citation: Gromala J, Jobanputra S. Prophylactic Vitamin D Prescribing for Adult Inpatients on Psychiatric Wards at Warneford Hospital – an Audit. BJPsych Open. 2025;11(S1):S239-S239. doi:10.1192/bjo.2025.10596.

audits.title: Evaluating Winter Vitamin D Supplementation and Deficiency in a Tier 4 CAMHS in Patient Unit: A Three-Cycle Audit
audits.standard: NICE: all CAMHS inpatients offered maintenance vitamin D supplementation from November to March

cycle1.result: 1 out of 10 inpatients received vitamin D supplementation; 5 had levels checked in past three months.

audits.intervention: 1:1 psychoeducation from a doctor and a clinic room poster promoting opportunistic vitamin D testing and supplementation.

cycle2.result: 9 out of 10 prescribed vitamin D (7 prophylaxis, 2 treatment doses); 5 had levels checked in past three months.

audits.other_findings: Three cycles: 9 out of 11 prescribed on 06/01/2025. Vitamin D level monitoring did not improve.
audits.citation: Mills B, Young L. Evaluating Winter Vitamin D Supplementation and Deficiency in a Tier 4 CAMHS in Patient Unit: A Three-Cycle Audit. BJPsych Open. 2025;11(S1):S257-S257. doi:10.1192/bjo.2025.10634.

audits.title: Walking on sunshine! Vitamin D in psychiatric inpatients
audits.standard: Local policies, RCPsych recommendations and NICE guidance on vitamin D
audits.setting: Local psychiatric inpatient hospital, Surrey and Borders NHS Foundation Trust

cycle1.result: 67% tested on admission; 39% of those tested had result recorded; 6/12 with low vitamin D correctly treated per NICE.

audits.intervention: Awareness raising and education for junior doctors with posters and communications.

cycle2.result: 75% tested on admission or during stay; 7/9 with low vitamin D correctly treated per NICE.

audits.other_findings: Nearly half had low vitamin D or were on treatment (48% then 58%).
audits.citation: Davies E, Mountford L. Walking on sunshine! Vitamin D in psychiatric inpatients. BJPsych Open. 2021;7(Suppl 1):S73-S74.

audits.title: Vitamin D monitoring and management in the inpatient services – reaudit
audits.standard: CKS Management of vitamin D deficiency or insufficiency in adults (2018), based on NOS and SACN guidance
audits.setting: Milford centre inpatient ward, Midlands Partnership NHS Trust

cycle1.result: 48/188 had vitamin D measured; 12/48 deficient or insufficient; 12/12 treated.

audits.intervention: Routine vitamin D testing on admission (stated as current practice).

cycle2.result: 90/115 had vitamin D measured; 43/90 insufficient or deficient; 22/43 (51%) had treatment documented.

audits.other_findings: Possible reasons for undocumented treatment included prescribing without notes documentation and discharge before results. Re-audit planned September 2021.
audits.citation: Krishnan V, Doyle C, Rusilowicz M. Vitamin D monitoring and management in the inpatient services – reaudit. BJPsych Open. 2021;7(Suppl 1):S86-S87.

audits.setting: Outpatients and inpatients, Scarborough General Hospital

cycle1.result: 64% met testing criteria (33% not documented); loading dose 50,000 IU for 6 weeks in 70%; follow-up vitamin D checked in only 53%.

audits.other_findings: GP advice omitted sunlight and dietary recommendations; 85% on calcium had it rechecked.

audits.title: Investigating Adherence to the 2022 NICE Vitamin D Management Guidelines on MHSOP (Mental Health Services for Older People) Wards
audits.standard: NICE 2022 vitamin D guidance: all patients tested on admission; all with level 50 or below prescribed vitamin D; calcium replaced if also deficient; specialist referral if eGFR <30, hypercalcaemia or granulomatous conditions
audits.setting: Two Mental Health Services for Older People (MHSOP) inpatient wards, Nottinghamshire Healthcare NHS Foundation Trust

cycle1.result: 30/34 (88%) tested on admission or had a recent level; 9 of 15 (60%) with insufficient or deficient levels prescribed vitamin D; 1 patient needing specialist referral not referred

audits.intervention: Vitamin D awareness poster on wards, meetings with the ward pharmacist and presentation at the local MHSOP clinical effectiveness meeting

cycle2.result: 31/33 (94%) tested on admission; 9 of 12 (75%) requiring prescription were prescribed vitamin D

audits.other_findings: Ongoing communication with pharmacists and rotating resident doctors was felt to be needed to sustain awareness.
audits.citation: Lee S. Investigating Adherence to the 2022 NICE Vitamin D Management Guidelines on MHSOP (Mental Health Services for Older People) Wards. BJPsych Open. 2025;11(Suppl 1):S253-S254.
